subject: MAP: performance evaluation & model-variant tradeoffs — close timeline

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@nimbus-analytics.com>; Tom Schultz <tom.schultz@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: performance evaluation & model-variant tradeoffs — close timeline

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our mutual action plan ask, I'm sending a concise execution plan for the performance evaluation you requested (latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency) and how we'll fold results back into the MAP and commercial close timeline. Goal: get you comfortable on perf + quality tradeoffs and have agreement to move to Dedicated capacity by the end of Q1.

High level MAP milestones (proposal):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize evaluation scope & dataset (shared) — owner: Nimbus + Redwood SEs
- Week 1: run baseline perf runs on 1xsession concurrency (target TTFT & p50/p95 latency)
- Week 2: stress/concurrency tests (4/8/16 concurrent sessions), throughput mapping
- Week 3: model variant quality runs (redwood catalog: base, quantized-8, trimmed-llm) + human eval for priority prompts
- Week 4: compile results, recommend serving config and economics (batching, cache profiles)

Deliverables attached: RID-MAP-v1.xlsx (timeline + owners + acceptance criteria). Connor will lead the perf harness; Priyom will coordinate the quality evals. Please confirm dataset access and whether Nimbus wants the runs in us-west or eu-central (we can mirror).

Close ask: if results meet the agreed SLOs (p95 < 400ms at target concurrency and acceptable quality delta < 3% on your eval set), we'd proceed to contract signature for a 12-month Dedicated commitment with the pricing shown in HS-4821.

Next steps: confirm dataset link, preferred region, and a target decision date (we suggested Mar 5 in the call).

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: MAP: performance evaluation & model-variant tradeoffs — close timeline

Elena / team —

I put together the perf harness plan and the initial test matrix. Attaching the high-level CSV of what we'll capture: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory footprint, GPU util, and KV cache hit rate. Key notes:

- Baselines will run against the same request set you provided (thanks). We'll seed with a 30s warmup per model variant to populate KV cache.
- Concurrency sweep: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 sessions. For each concurrency point we'll run 300 sequences of your median prompt length (and 50 long-tail sequences).
- Model variants to test (from Redwood catalog):
  * rdx-13b-base (float16) — highest quality, reference latency
  * rdx-13b-q8 (quantized int8) — lower memory, slight perf gain
  * rdx-7b-trimmed (small param set) — best throughput, lower quality on long-context tasks

Acceptance criteria we propose to include in the MAP sheet: p95 latency at target concurrency < 400ms, TTFT < 120ms for interactive flows, and quality delta (relative to rdx-13b-base) <= 3% for top-line intents. If a variant fails quality but meets perf/economics we flag it as "latency-first option" for non-interactive routes.

I'll run the first batch in us-west-2 unless you request eu-central. Results (raw CSV + summary PDF) will be posted to the shared link.

Connor
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

Thanks Soojin / Connor —

Dataset access confirmed (shared S3 link sent to Connor). Nimbus prefers runs in us-west to reflect our production region. Decision date of Mar 5 works for our procurement calendar. One request: can you include an evaluation column for "regression on entity extraction" since that's our most mission-critical quality metric?

We're fine with your acceptance criteria but would like an additional check for TTFT under cold-start (no cache) and warm-start. Also, please flag any model variant that requires a >15% increase in GPU count to meet throughput — procurement needs that number for cost modeling.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Gomez
Director of Engineering, Nimbus Analytics
elena.gomez@nimbus-analytics.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>; Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: performance evaluation & model-variant tradeoffs — close timeline

Elena / team —

We ran the scheduled sweep last week in us-west-2. Summary highlights below (full CSV attached to this thread):

- rdx-13b-base (float16): p50=110ms, p95=410ms, TTFT=135ms (cold), 98% entity-extraction F1 on your eval set. Requires baseline GPU count = 8 per pool to hit 120 concurrent requests at p95 ~420ms.
- rdx-13b-q8 (quantized int8): p50=95ms, p95=310ms, TTFT=125ms (cold), 96% F1. Memory reduction ~30% vs base. Achieves 120 concurrent requests with 6 GPUs.
- rdx-7b-trimmed: p50=65ms, p95=220ms, TTFT=110ms (cold), 92% F1. Best throughput (tokens/sec) and lowest GPU usage (4 GPUs for 120 concurrent).

Interpretation and recommendation:
- If Nimbus prioritizes strict entity-extraction quality (F1 >= 97%), rdx-13b-base is the safe choice but has higher infra requirement and p95 slightly above our desired 400ms threshold at high concurrency (we can tighten with prefix caching or slightly larger pool).
- rdx-13b-q8 delivers a strong balance: quality within ~2% of base, p95 well under 400ms, and lower GPU footprint (economics win).
- rdx-7b-trimmed is attractive for cost and throughput where a 5–6% quality delta is acceptable (batching, summarization, or non-critical chat).

We've attached perf-results-20260227.csv and model-variant-eval-notes.pdf with the per-prompt breakdown and recommendations for serving config (batching windows, local KV cache TTL).

Next in MAP: sign-off on the recommended variant(s) for the pilot and approval to provision Dedicated capacity for the pilot week (we estimate 6–8 GPUs depending on variant). If you agree, Soojin can route to procurement and legal to finalize terms.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachments: perf-results-20260227.csv, model-variant-eval-notes.pdf

Subject: Re: MAP: performance evaluation & model-variant tradeoffs — close timeline

Elena —

Appreciate the quick turn and the clear asks. Based on Priyom's readout and your tolerance:

- Proposal for pilot: provision Dedicated pool sized for rdx-13b-q8 (6 GPUs) for a 2-week pilot (start Feb 15). This gives you p95 headroom and keeps unit cost close to your target.
- If post-pilot quality regression is <2% vs base we'll proceed to the 12-month commit (deal HS-4821) with the pricing in the MAP sheet.
- I'll kick procurement and legal today; please confirm who at Nimbus will OK the pilot PO (name + email) and whether DocuSign review can proceed in parallel.

Connor / Marcus: please prep a short runbook for the pilot handoff (on-call, telemetry links, and rollback plan). Marcus — can you post the runbook link in the HS-4821 HubSpot record?

Elena — once we have the PO contact, I'll create the DocuSign package and target signature by Feb 12 so provisioning can start Feb 15.

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
